items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: So I took the thing and Gene Tobin was in... I gave Gene the grant request and had him read it on the red eye coming back here... Gene’s been wonderful throughout this.

ctx.x: Well I wanted to talk a little bit more about your faithfulness and your support of Hamilton College and I’m impressed by the group of men from your class and from others back then who have had a lifelong commitment to this college. Can you explain why?

I’ve often wondered. The people here did a terrific job of injecting us all with some kind of fluid. We came out of here thinking Hamilton is a wonderful place, and we never changed that viewpoint. I can’t understand for example my own kids, who went to other schools, which I would consider the same kind of school, small and so on, and they don’t give a damn. They don’t give them any money, they don’t care. I just don’t understand, I say why don’t you ever go back? They’re just not interested. They got an…

down to Ithaca and toured Cornell. My God. You can’t even move. You can’t park your car, you can’t do anything. And I thought what a difference, what a difference. I think it’s the type of college, and I’d be surprised if it isn’t duplicated in schools like Williams and Amherst and so on. I think it’s the attitude and the life you lead with the school, the relationship between you and the school. The fact that, Gene Tobin has a thing over here every week for the kids to come talk to him. I mean that doesn’t exist…
